label: copy phase of long sequences: early recalls or z/digit/w/t inputs
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L). It never fires in the original phase, and fires on the delimiter only 14 times. It is strongly biased toward long sequences (L=9 holds 64% of activation mass, L=8 holds 25%, nothing for L<=4). Within the copy phase it fires most on the first copy steps (recall_idx 1-2, i.e. to_go 6-7 in long sequences; 61% of mass) and again near the end of long sequences, and on particular fed-back input tokens: z (26% rate), the digits 2/0/1, w and t. The largest activations come when z or a digit is the first token being copied (recall_idx 1). Activation is graded and depends on the token mix, so the predicate is incomplete: dev F1 0.58, mass recall 0.80. Many z/digit steps in shorter or mid-sequence positions do not fire, and some activations land on other letters.
